cites.quote: 'I arrived at the conclusion that Mr. Menachem Begin has more chances than any other candidate to form the next government -- that is, 61 Knesset members spoke out in favor of his forming the government.
Begin has support in principle from three religious parties -- the National Religious Party, the Tami Party and the Agudat Israel Party -- which hold a total of 13 seats in the Knesset (parliament).
Aharon Abu Hatzeira's Tami faction, with three seats, indicated to Navon that it preferred a government headed by Begin, while Moshe Dayan's two-seat Telem party leaned toward Labor
ב-10 ביולי זימן נבון את סיעות הבית להתייעצויות ב-13 וב-14 ביולי

notes: Partial: President Navon stated that 61 MKs backed Begin (Likud 48 + NRP 6 + Agudat Yisrael 4 + Tami 3, the parties UPI names). What the Alignment, Hadash, Tehiya, Telem, Shinui and Ratz told the President is not stated as a recommendation in the sources retrieved (JTA describes leanings only), so they are 'not stated', not 'no recommendation'.

Mandate given to Begin on 15 July 1981 (Navon's letter is dated 16 July in the State Archives account). UPI's 1981 pages returned 403 to a direct request on 2026-11-05; their quotes are from a search-index extract. The State Archives chapter also returned 403; its quote is from a search-index extract.

events.textEn: President Navon consulted the factions on 13–14 July.

events.textEn: Navon tasked Begin with forming a government; the State Archives dates the letter to 16 July.

cites.quote: formally summoned by President Yitzhak Navon today to form a new government

notes: Press-based event date 15 July retained with dispute. The JTA item is published 16 July and says today; its original dateline was not recovered. The State Archives describes the formal presidential letter as dated 16 July. Do not infer separate appointment events.

values.value: 15 July 1981 in the existing JTA/UPI research
16 July 1981 presidential letter in the State Archives account

conflicts.resolution: Unresolved after targeted primary-source retrieval. Contemporary press identifies 15 July, while the State Archives describes a letter of 16 July; the JTA 16 July publication date cannot determine its dispatch dateline. The original letter and President’s diary are the deciding records: Israel State Archives file נ-571/13 pp.5–7 (letter), and נ-224/4 (diary/consultations). Archive catalogue returned HTTP 403 and original JTA PDF transport failed; no second mandate event is invented.

term.inclusionRule: At least two independently authored qualifying chronologies, including one official or academic, plus direct support for the date. The Knesset and MFA histories count separately; the JVL mirror is not another independent source. Formal government succession steps are recorded separately in formation.events.

events.textEn: Israel completed its withdrawal from the Sinai Peninsula under the peace treaty with Egypt.
events.textHe: ישראל השלימה את נסיגתה מחצי האי סיני במסגרת הסכם השלום עם מצרים.

cites.quote: the withdrawal from the Sinai was completed with the evacuation of Yamit
Israel’s three-stage withdrawal from Sinai Peninsula completed

events.textEn: Israel launched Operation Peace for Galilee against PLO terrorist bases in Lebanon in June 1982, beginning the First Lebanon War.
events.textHe: ישראל פתחה במבצע שלום הגליל נגד בסיסי טרור של אש״ף בלבנון ביוני 1982, עם תחילת מלחמת לבנון הראשונה.

cites.quote: PLO terrorist strongholds in Lebanon used for attacks against northern Israel
which began in June 1982
Operation Peace for Galilee

notes: MFA’s chronology identifies PLO terrorist strongholds used for attacks against northern Israel. Its 1985 withdrawal is described separately under k11 and retained a security zone; no single ceasefire endpoint is inferred.
לפי ציר הזמן של משרד החוץ, בסיסי הטרור של אש״ף שימשו לתקיפות על צפון ישראל. הנסיגה ב־1985, תוך השארת רצועת ביטחון, מתוארת בנפרד בכנסת ה־11 ואינה מוצגת כמועד הפסקת אש.

events.textEn: Bank shares collapsed, and the government closed the stock market for two weeks.
events.textHe: מניות הבנקים קרסו, והממשלה סגרה את הבורסה לשבועיים.

cites.quote: the collapse of the bank shares took place
in October 1983, after the collapse of the bank shares
the government ordered the closing down of the stock market for two weeks.

candidatesPending.label: Sabra and Shatila massacre and Kahan inquiry
candidatesPending.why: Both Knesset history and MFA timeline select the massacre and inquiry. The candidate bundles September 1982 killings with the 1983 report. Knesset history also misdates appointment of the inquiry to November 1982. Split the acts and inspect direct dates before promotion.

candidatesPending.label: Bus 300 affair
candidatesPending.why: Both Knesset history and MFA timeline select the 1984 bus affair/hijacking. The candidate needs to distinguish the hijacking from the later killing/disclosure acts and verify their direct dates.

endedBy.textEn: The Knesset enacted a dissolution law; the next election was held on 23 July 1984.
endedBy.textHe: הכנסת חוקקה חוק התפזרות; הבחירות הבאות נערכו ב־23 ביולי 1984.

cites.quote: dissolution law on 4 April 1984
20 ביולי 1981 – 13 באוגוסט 1984

gaps: Results notice YP 2727 signed 9 July 1981 is retained; the official OData snapshot has 120 opening members starting 20 July 1981.
Formation timeline is a sourced subset; missing steps must not be inferred from statutory maximum periods.
First-government coalition membership is confirmed by the four-faction agreement announced in the 5 August 1981 plenum, PDF p. 1; Agudat Yisrael was a coalition party without ministers.
Recommendation evidence and caveats are inherited from docs/research/pm-recommendations-1977-2006.md; a source quoting the President is not an original presidential record.

Original 1981 presidential letter remains uninspected; the tasking-day versus letter-date discrepancy is preserved. Government 19 ended when government 20 was invested on 10 October 1983, verified in the plenum record.
